title: Chapter 70 — Market Intelligence
intro: Gathering and using competitive and market intelligence to protect and grow your trade book.

sections.title: What to Track
sections.content:
Who are your competitors' trade reps? What accounts do they serve? What are their pricing tiers? When does their rep visit job sites? What brands do they push hardest?

You do not need a spy network. You need to listen. Builders talk. Designers mention who else they work with. Delivery crews see competitor products on job sites. Your own salespeople hear competitor names from retail customers. Aggregate these signals and you have a competitive map.

Also track market trends: building permit volumes trending up or down, new developments announced, builder acquisitions or closures, design trends shifting toward specific brands or categories. The rep who sees the market shifting before others do has a first-mover advantage.

sections.title: Using Intelligence
sections.content:
Competitive intelligence informs your strategy. If your competitor just lost their trade rep, their accounts are vulnerable for 60-90 days. Prospect them now.

If a builder is unhappy with their current supplier's delivery performance, that is your wedge. Reference your delivery track record without naming the competitor: 'We have a 98 percent on-time delivery rate for trade accounts. I would love to show you how that works on your next project.'

If design trends are shifting toward European brands and your competitor does not carry them, lead with those brands in your prospecting. Your product portfolio is a competitive weapon — use it.

sections.title: Intelligence Sharing
sections.content:
Share relevant intelligence with your team. If a competitor is offering aggressive pricing to win a specific builder, your trade desk needs to know before they get undercut on a quote.

Create a simple monthly update for your manager: key account movements, competitive activity, market trends, and prospecting opportunities. This positions you as the trade channel expert in your organization and keeps leadership aligned with your strategy.
